applies_why: The judge text compares the challenger's and defender's chains by noting both are footed, which is the chain-against-chain collision K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: by footing, never verse by verse—reading it as allowing chain-level footing comments versus forbidding any mention of what a chain names; I used the first because the judge expressly says both chains are footed.
why: The judge weighs the two chains by stating each is footed and does not rely on the retired no-contrary-stating-verse test.
